criteria.description: Fidelity to source - sentence-by-sentence verification: abstract must not invent or misattribute facts, numbers, or references. Defects include merging results from different objects, upgrading ongoing work to completed results, adding numeric ranges not in body (e.g., channel counts 118/128, 98 common, 43 experiments, 20 channels <0.5%, voxel 5x5x5 mm, 29x34x24, cluster 13 at p=0.001), or stating conclusions not confirmed in text.

Coverage of problem, method and findings - abstract must convey: problem of heterogeneous EEG data from equipment/software updates (Neuroscan vs Brain Products) and need to reuse open components; method as MATLAB-scripts pipeline using EEGLAB, sLORETA for 3D reconstruction, spherical spline interpolation for lost channels, unification by intersection, and multilevel mediation analysis; and that approach was approbated on social interaction experiments. Vague generic abstract with no concrete findings scores low.

Appropriate uncertainty and caveats - abstract must not omit or upgrade caveats stated in body: manual artifact removal still more accurate than automatic, interpolation limited by number of lost channels and reduces significance if many restored, non-matching channels excluded due to distortion (~20%). Must not present interpolation or reconstruction as perfect or fully automated without human factor.

Coherent abstract structure and length compliance - abstract must be in Russian only, single paragraph, logical flow problem->method->result, ~51 words. Exceeding target by >30% (~67+ words) must lose points scaled to overshoot. Copying source tokenization spacing is minor presentation only, not a content defect.
